title: Deterministic complexity of equality at $n = 0$
statement:
Let $\mathrm{equality}_0 \colon \mathrm{BoolInput}\,0 \times \mathrm{BoolInput}\,0 \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be the equality function on $0$-bit Boolean inputs, and let $D(\mathrm{equality}_0)$ denote its deterministic communication complexity, that is, the infimum over all deterministic two-party protocols computing it of the worst-case number of bits exchanged, taken in $\bbn_\infty$. Then
\[
  D(\mathrm{equality}_0) = 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: complexity measured as the deterministic communication complexity D (infimum over computing protocols, valued in ENat)
replaced:
When $n = 0$ both inputs are the unique empty string, so the equality function
is constantly \texttt{true} and requires zero communication:
\[
  D(\mathrm{equality}_0) = 0.
\]
